chunks: And he (the narrator) asked him also about an Imam who became busy/distracted, so he turned away, and did not appoint anyone else; what is the state of the people? He said:
"There is no prayer for them except with an Imam, so let one of them step forward, and through him complete what remains of it, and their prayer will be considered complete."
ai.seo_question: What happens to the congregation's prayer if the Imam gets distracted and leaves without appointing a new leader?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for congregational prayer when the Imam is interrupted (*ahdatha*) and departs without appointing a successor, establishing that the prayer remains valid rather than requiring a restart. It instructs the congregation to appoint one of their own to complete the remaining portions, reflecting the Shia principle of continuity in communal worship. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining the unity of the prayer (*jamāʿah*) even in the absence of a designated leader.
